newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 4.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 4.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising,
Marketing, Media & the Internet and Brand-name Products.

LONDON - British Telecommunications Plc is expected to announce an alliance with Japan's Fujitsu Ltd and France's Alcatel that could revolutionise the telephone network, the Sunday Telegraph says. The venture will allow BT to carry video and Internet services on enhanced telephone lines. The link-up with the two companies is expected to be announced later this month. (Reuter)

PARIS - French broadcasting regulator Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA) says Lagardere Group's radio stations cover a population bigger than that allowed by law since the regrouping of its interests in Hachette Filipacchi Medias. Lagardere, which contests this, may have to sell RFM or Skyrock. (La Tribune)

PARIS - Private television channel M6 says it was justified in refusing to carry adverts promoting pay television station Canal Plus because Canal Plus's hours of uncoded broadcasting compete directly with M6 both for advertising and programming. (La Tribune)

PARIS - Car sales in France fell 9.7 percent in July, the seventh consecutive monthly fall from inflated 1996 levels, but Renault sales advanced against the trend, the French carmakers' committee CCFA says. Renault says its Megane, Clio and Twingo models were the three best sellers in France last month. Car industry analysts are beginning to discern a rebound in the French automotive sector following a 20 percent fall this year in car sales. (Reuter)
PARIS - Hypermarkets are following the lead of entrepreneur Edouard Leclerc and cutting petrol prices, re-igniting a price war with service stations. (Le Parisien)

PARIS - The French GSM mobile phone market, the biggest mobile communications segment in France, grew 9.5 percent in June to total 3.39 million subscribers, says ART, the French telecommunications regulator. The figures confirm claims in July by the three main companies operating in the GSM market that June had been a record month for sales. (Reuter)

PARIS - A $2.5 billion gamble by European Airbus Industrie pays off as two high-profile airlines say they will order a new stretched model of its A340 long-range passenger jet. In separate announcements, Britain's Virgin Atlantic Airways and Air Canada say they will be launch customers for the A340-600 widebody jet, Airbus's challenge to Boeing Co's monopoly of the high-capacity segment. (Reuter)
PARIS - An Emporio Armani boutique which was due to open in October in the famous drugstore on Boulevard St Germain will now not open until January 1998. (Le Parisien)
